subject: AUDIT/bug (serious, sibling of #111): mutate-gate can leave the WORKING TREE MUTATED and still report 'ok caught' and exit 0. Live 2026-08-16: two 'mv: cannot stat task-store.sh.mutbak' lines went to stderr, the restore silently failed, and lib/task-store.sh was left emitting newline-separated paths against a NUL-expecting reader — companion_open_tasks returned NOTHING, i.e. the entire carried-task resume path was dead in the tree while the gate said green. The mv failure is unchecked and two restore paths (the per-mutation mv and the EXIT trap's find) race for the same .mutbak
done_when: a restore that does not put the file back byte-for-byte FAILS the gate loudly (checksum the target before mutating and verify after restoring); the two restore paths cannot race or the loser is harmless; a test proves a failed restore is reported rather than swallowed
context: dev/mutate-gate.sh (_mut_restore's find, the per-mutation cp/mv around line 110-147), and #111 (the stale lock) — same root: the gate's own crash-safety is the one thing it never verifies
